name: National Gallery of Art
tagline: The only Leonardo painting in the Americas, a free Calder mobile, a sculpture garden.
description: One of the world's great encyclopedic art museums and entirely free. The West Building (John Russell Pope, 1941) holds the European and American old masters; the East Building (I. M. Pei, 1978) holds modern and contemporary. A separate sculpture garden across 7th Street.
hours_summary: Mon–Sat 10 AM – 5 PM · Sun 11 AM – 6 PM
review_long:
The West Building's painting galleries are arranged chronologically by national school — Italian, Flemish, Dutch, French, Spanish — and include Ginevra de' Benci, the only Leonardo da Vinci painting on permanent display in the Americas. The East Building has a permanent Calder mobile in the atrium and rotating modern exhibitions.

Free, including the major special exhibitions. The sculpture garden adds a whole half-day in good weather.

tips.text: Always free. So is the sculpture garden across 7th Street.

highlights.item: Ginevra de' Benci, Leonardo da Vinci

distance_landmark: On the National Mall, between 4th and 7th
